title: Why do we brush our teeth?
examples: Teacher, what happens if I don't brush my teeth?
Are there really tiny bad things on my teeth?
How long should I brush my teeth for?

explain.say: Your teeth need to stay clean to stay strong.

draw.text: Why do we brush our teeth?

explain.say: A sticky film called plaque grows on your teeth.
Plaque is made by tiny germs that you cannot see.
The germs can make small holes in your teeth. These holes are called cavities.

draw.text: Germs can make holes in teeth

explain.say: Brushing takes away the sticky plaque and germs.
After sweet snacks, plaque grows faster. Brush in the morning and before bed.

faq.q: Why do I need to brush my teeth?
faq.a: You brush your teeth to keep them clean and strong. Plaque builds up and tiny germs can make holes in your teeth.
asks: What is the purpose of brushing?
Should I brush my teeth every day?

faq.a: Plaque is a sticky film that forms on your teeth. It is made up of germs that love to stick around.
asks: Is plaque bad for my teeth?

faq.a: Yes. Germs are far too small to see without a microscope.
You should brush for about two minutes every morning and night. This gives enough time to clean all spots.
asks: How many times a day should I brush?

faq.q: What happens if I don't brush?
faq.a: Plaque builds up, and the germs can make small holes called cavities. A dentist can help if a tooth feels sore.
asks: What is the result of not brushing?

facts: Plaque is a sticky film that forms on teeth.
Germs are the tiny things that make plaque.
Brushing helps remove plaque and germs.
Brushing helps keep teeth strong and healthy.

quiz.say: What is the sticky film that grows on teeth?
quiz.why: Plaque is a sticky film of germs on your teeth.

wrong.0: Toothpaste is what you brush with, to clean the film away.
wrong.1: Cavities are small holes, and the film comes first.

quiz.say: What can germs in plaque do to your teeth?
quiz.why: Germs in plaque can make small holes called cavities.

wrong.1: Brushing keeps teeth strong, and germs harm them.
wrong.2: Clean teeth look shiny, and germs make them dull.

quiz.say: What does brushing take away from your teeth?

options.show: the hard part of your teeth
options.say: the hard part of your teeth

quiz.why: Brushing sweeps away plaque and the germs in it.

wrong.0: Brushing cleans your teeth, and their colour stays the same.
wrong.2: The hard outside of your teeth stays, and brushing protects it.
